question.value: Investigate the chemical composition of four FUor-like Class I YSOs and compare their COM abundances with other YSOs.

evidence.quote: Our aim is to investigate the chemical composition of four FUor-like Class I YSOs: L1551 IRS 5, Haro 5a IRS, V346 Nor, and OO Ser, and to compare their abundances of COMs with other YSOs in the literature.
The four FUor-like sources were observed as part of the ALMA program 2016.1.00209.S (PI: Takami) in Cycle 4.
We search for COMs line emission in ALMA Band 6 observations.

evidence.quote: For L1551 IRS 5 these were 4.6, 3.6, and 11.3 minutes for the 7m, C40-3 and C40-6 arrays, respectively.
In the case of Haro 5a IRS these were 4.1, 3.1 and 9.3 minutes, respectively, with the 7m and C40-6 observations being repeated due to weather conditions.

method.value: CASSIS MCMC synthetic spectra fit N, Tex, vLSR, FWHM and source size using selected unblended lines with sufficient SNR.

evidence.quote: We used the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach provided in CASSIS for our analysis.

Each synthetic spectrum is created using a combination of column density ($N$), excitation temperature ($T_\mathrm{ex}$), systemic velocity ($v_\mathrm{LSR}$), FWHM of the line, and source size ($s$).
A $\chi^2$ is computed for all the transitions selected for the comparison (meaning lines that are not blended and with sufficient SNR).

referee_caveats_inferred: Reported North methanol column densities exceed the stated MCMC upper bound of 10^19 cm−2; the actual bounds need clarification.
The V346 Nor CH3CHO fitted velocity of −5.46 km s−1 lies outside its stated −5.0 to −2.0 km s−1 search interval.
The CH2DOH paragraph reverses the apparent high-opacity versus low-opacity temperature comparison relative to the table and preceding description.
The spectroscopy paragraph names CHD2OH, whereas the fitting analysis concerns CH2DOH; verify the actual database entry.
OO Ser is described as having six COMs, but its fitted table lists five; C2H5CN appears inconsistently in the morphology discussion.
The additional-pixel discussion lists CH3C15N among both nondetections and fitted detections.
The stated 0.16, 0.50 and 0.84 percentiles require clarification as literal percentiles versus quantiles.
Fixed shared temperatures and sizes can suppress apparent uncertainties in column-density ratios.
No quantitative convergence diagnostic or homogeneous statistical test of the eruptive/quiescent difference is provided.

missing_for_reproduction: Raw-data public-access status and downloadable calibrated/image-product inventory are not stated.
Calibration, self-calibration, continuum subtraction and imaging scripts are not provided in the supplied text.
The hosted transition-selection table and spectral-fit appendices are needed to reconstruct exact fitting inputs.
CASSIS configuration, database snapshots, complete fixed-parameter sets and explicit priors are missing.
Several reported parameter bounds and species identifications require reconciliation with the result tables.
Numerical imaging geometry, moment integration intervals and additional extraction coordinates are missing.
reproducibility.score_reason: On a 0–10 scale: project code, software, imaging weighting, fitting strategy and numerical answer keys are detailed, but calibration/imaging settings, exact fitting inputs and public-data status are incomplete; internal inconsistencies need resolution.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results are numeric, but the supplied text does not establish public ALMA access and leaves essential processing and fitting settings unresolved.
